claims.text: MOA: bactericidal; enters the cell and disrupts DNA and inhibits DNA synth.
claims.quote: Metronidazole is a bactericidal antibiotic. It enters bacterial cell walls and disrupts DNA and inhibits DNA synthesis in certain microorganisms.

claims.text: Treats: all obligate anaerobes (⍉facultative or aerobic bacteria) and protozoa (Trichomonas, E. histolytica, Giardia).
claims.quote: Metronidazole is active against All obligate anaerobic bacteria (it is inactive against facultative anaerobic and aerobic bacteria) Certain protozoan parasites (eg, Trichomonas vaginalis, Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia intestinalis [lamblia])

claims.text: Know: abx of choice for BV; often combined w other abx for anaerobic infections.
claims.quote: Metronidazole is used primarily for infections caused by obligate anaerobes, often with other antimicrobials. Metronidazole is the antibiotic of choice for bacterial vaginosis.

claims.text: Know: C. diff: ⍉longer first-line; only for mild cases when vanco and fidaxomicin are unavailable, or IV w vanco for severe cases.
claims.quote: No longer recommended as a first-line antibiotic Should be considered only for mild cases when vancomycin and fidaxomicin are unavailable, or given IV in combination with vancomycin for severe cases

claims.text: Know: well absorbed PO (IV only if PO ⍉poss); good CSF penetration.
claims.quote: Oral metronidazole is absorbed well. It is usually given IV only if patients cannot be treated orally. It is distributed widely in body fluids and penetrates into cerebrospinal fluid, resulting in high concentrations.

claims.text: CI: prior allergic rxn to it.
claims.quote: Metronidazole and tinidazole are contraindicated in patients who have had an allergic reaction to it.

claims.text: Preg: some experts ⍉it in the first trimester (cleft lip reported in some studies), though CDC allows a single dose for trichomoniasis @ any stage; ⍉recommended while breastfeed.
claims.quote: Most human studies have not shown increased risk of cancer, birth defects, or other fetal adverse effects after use of metronidazole during pregnancy; however, in some studies, cleft lip (with or without cleft palate) was reported in neonates of women who took metronidazole during the first trimester. Some experts advise avoiding metronidazole during the first trimester, although the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) 2021 sexually transmitted infections treatment guidelines indicate that a single 2-g dose can be used at any stage of pregnancy to treat trichomoniasis. Metronidazole enters breast milk; use during breastfeeding is not recommended.
claims.locator: Use of Metronidazole and Tinidazole During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Caution: GI upset; CNS effects (HA, seizures) and periph neuropathy; disulfiram-like rxn if EToH = taken w.in 3 days; metallic taste, dark urine.
claims.quote: Nausea, vomiting, headache, seizures, syncope, other central nervous system effects, and peripheral neuropathy can occur; rash, fever, and reversible neutropenia have been reported. A disulfiram-like reaction (including flushing, headache, nausea, and vomiting) may occur if alcohol is ingested within 3 days of use. Metronidazole can cause a metallic taste and dark urine.
claims.locator: Adverse Effects of Metronidazole and Tinidazole

claims.text: Caution: ↑ warfarin effect; dose USU ↓in sig liver dz (⍉in renal failure).
claims.quote: Metronidazole and tinidazole doses are not decreased in patients with renal failure. Metronidazole doses are usually decreased 50% in patients with significant liver disease; tinidazole has not been studied in liver disease and should be used with caution if at all. Metronidazole and tinidazole inhibit metabolism of warfarin and may increase its anticoagulant effect.
claims.locator: Dosing Considerations for Metronidazole and Tinidazole

claims.text: Tinidazole: related nitroimidazole, similar mech, more limited use.
claims.quote: Tinidazole is a related nitroimidazole with similar mechanism of action but more limited clinical use.

claims.text: Tinidazole: mainly for the protozoa (Trichomonas, E. histolytica, Giardia); ⍉for systemic anaerobic infections.
claims.quote: Tinidazole is used primarily for the protozoan parasites mentioned above. It is not used for systemic anaerobic bacterial infections.

claims.text: Tinidazole: longer ½ life than metronidazole (less freq dosing).
claims.quote: Tinidazole has a slightly longer half-life than metronidazole, allowing for less frequent dosing.

claims.text: Know: giardiasis: tinidazole, metronidazole, secnidazole or nitazoxanide; tx failure and resistance can occur w any.
claims.quote: For symptomatic giardiasis, tinidazole, metronidazole, secnidazole, or nitazoxanide are used. Treatment failures and resistance can occur with any of them.

claims.text: Preg: tinidazole = avoided in preg (animal studies suggest mod risk); defer breastfeed for 72 h after a single dose.
claims.quote: There are limited data on use of tinidazole during pregnancy, but because animal studies suggest moderate risk, tinidazole is avoided during pregnancy. Breastfeeding should be deferred for 72 hours after a single 2-g oral dose of tinidazole.
claims.locator: Use of Metronidazole and Tinidazole During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Caution: tinidazole: ↑ warfarin effect; ⍉studied in liver dz (use w caution, if @ all).
claims.quote: tinidazole has not been studied in liver disease and should be used with caution if at all. Metronidazole and tinidazole inhibit metabolism of warfarin and may increase its anticoagulant effect.
claims.locator: Dosing Considerations for Metronidazole and Tinidazole
